title: नेपालको राष्ट्रिय विकासका लागि सुरक्षा व्यवस्थापन Nepalko Rastriya Bikaska lagi Surakshya Byabasthapan
nepali: समृद्धिको पूर्वसर्त विकास र विकासको आधार सुरक्षा हो । विकासको अपेक्षाकृत सफलता प्रभावकारी सुरक्षा व्यवस्थाबाट मात्र सुनिश्चित हुन्छ । सुरक्षा र विकासमा एकअर्काको अन्तरनिर्भरताले मात्र राष्ट्रिय लक्ष्य प्राप्ति गर्न सकिन्छ । विकासमा सुरक्षाको योगदानलाई दुइवटा आधारबाट हेर्न सकिन्छ≤ पहिलो, विकासका हरेक चरणमा सुरक्षा संयन्त्रको अपेक्षाकृत व्यवस्थापन र दोस्रोमा, सुरक्षा संयन्त्रको नेतृत्व, व्यवस्थापन र अगुवाइमा गरिने विकास । विकासमा सुरक्षाको पूर्ण प्रत्याभूतिले स्वदेशी तथा वैदेशिक लगानीलाई विकासमा आकर्षण र सञ्चालनमा सहजता प्रदान गर्दछ । सुरक्षा संयन्त्रलाई राष्ट्रिय विकास प्रणालीमा आवद्ध गर्न सकेमा पूर्वाधार, ऊर्जा, सडक यातायात, पुनर्निर्माण, सीपजस्ता क्षेत्रमा दिगो र गुणस्तरीय विकासको प्रचुर सम्भावना देखिन्छ । संविधान, क्षेत्रगत कानुनहरु, पन्ध्रौं योजना, वजेट, राष्ट्रिय नीति तथा कार्यक्रमहरुले राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षालाई विकाससँग अन्तरआवद्ध गरेमा मात्र विकासले सार्थक र अपेक्षित लक्ष्य प्राप्त गर्न सक्ने कुरालाई जोड दिएको देखिन्छ । नेपालले वि. सं. २१०० सम्म प्राप्त गर्ने गरी राखेको समृद्ध नेपाल निर्माणको दीर्घकालीन सोंचको सहज प्राप्तिका लागि राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षा र विकासलाई एक रथका दुई पांग्राका रुपमा लिने गरी नीति तथा कार्यक्रमको अवलम्वन गर्नुपर्ने हुन्छ । सुरक्षा नभएको विकास र विकास नभएको सुरक्षाले मुलुक निर्माण र नागरिक अपेक्षा पूरा गर्न कुनै अर्थ नराख्ने हु“दा दुवै क्षेत्रको तादात्म्यताले मात्र राष्ट्रिय सोंच र लक्ष्य प्राप्ति सहज हुने देखिन्छ ।
american_english: Development is the precondition of prosperity, and security is the foundation of development. The relative success of development is assured only by an effective security arrangement. National goals can be attained only through the interdependence of security and development. The contribution of security to development can be viewed from two bases: first, the appropriate management of the security apparatus at every stage of development, and second, development carried out under the leadership, management and guidance of the security apparatus. A complete guarantee of security in development provides attraction for domestic and foreign investment in development and ease in its operation. If the security apparatus can be tied into the national development system, ample possibilities for sustainable and quality development are seen in sectors such as infrastructure, energy, road transport, reconstruction and skills. The constitution, sectoral laws, the Fifteenth Plan, the budget, and national policies and programs appear to stress that development can reach meaningful and expected targets only if national security is interlinked with development. For the easy attainment of the long-term vision of building a prosperous Nepal that Nepal has set to achieve by 2100 BS, policies and programs must be adopted that treat national security and development as the two wheels of one chariot. Since development without security and security without development have no meaning for nation-building and for fulfilling citizens' expectations, it appears that only identification of the two sectors with each other will make the attainment of the national vision and goals easy.

The contribution of security to development may be regarded from two standpoints: first, the appropriate management of the security apparatus at every stage of development, and second, development undertaken under the leadership, management and guidance of the security apparatus. A full guarantee of security in development affords attraction to domestic and foreign investment in development and facility in its operation. If the security apparatus can be attached to the national development system, abundant prospects for sustainable and qualitative development are apparent in sectors such as infrastructure, energy, road transport, reconstruction and skills. The constitution, sectoral laws, the Fifteenth Plan, the budget and national policies and programmes would appear to emphasise that development can achieve meaningful and expected objectives only if national security is interlinked with development. For the ready attainment of the long-term vision of building a prosperous Nepal that Nepal has set itself to achieve by 2100 BS, policies and programmes must be adopted that regard national security and development as the two wheels of a single chariot. Inasmuch as development without security and security without development bear no meaning for nation-building and for the fulfilment of citizens' expectations, it appears that only a harmonisation of the two spheres will render the attainment of the national vision and objectives easy.
australian_english: Development is the precondition for prosperity and security is the bedrock of development. The relative success of development is only assured by an effective security set-up. National goals can only be reached through security and development depending on each other. You can look at what security contributes to development from two angles: first, managing the security apparatus properly at every stage of development, and second, development carried out under the leadership, management and guidance of the security apparatus. A full guarantee of security in development pulls domestic and foreign investment into development and makes it easier to run. If the security apparatus can be hooked into the national development system, there's plenty of scope for sustainable, quality development in areas like infrastructure, energy, road transport, reconstruction and skills. The constitution, sectoral laws, the Fifteenth Plan, the budget and national policies and programs look to be putting the weight on this: development can only hit meaningful and expected targets if national security is interlinked with development. To easily get to the long-term vision of a prosperous Nepal that Nepal has set itself to reach by 2100 BS, policies and programs have to be taken up that treat national security and development as two wheels of the one cart. Since development without security and security without development count for nothing when it comes to building the country and meeting what citizens expect, it looks like only the two areas being at one will make getting to the national vision and goals easy.
informal_english: Ja, development is what you need before prosperity, and security is the base of development. Development only really comes off when security is properly sorted. You'll only nail the national goals if security and development lean on each other. There are two ways to look at what security does for development: first, managing the security set-up properly at every stage of development, and second, development that happens under the security set-up's leadership, management and guidance. When security in development is fully guaranteed, local and foreign investors get pulled in and things run a lot easier. If the security set-up can be roped into the national development system, there's heaps of room for lasting, quality development in things like infrastructure, energy, road transport, rebuilding and skills. The constitution, sectoral laws, the Fifteenth Plan, the budget and national policies and programmes seem to be making the point that development will only hit the goals that matter if national security is tied in with development. To get to that long-term dream of a prosperous Nepal that Nepal has set for itself by 2100 BS without hassle, we need policies and programmes that treat national security and development like the two wheels of one wagon. Because development with no security, and security with no development, means nothing for building the country and giving citizens what they expect, it looks like only the two pulling together will make the national vision and goals easy to reach.
